card.name: Reng
card.era: codified Qajar era (19th c.); older roots
card.tagline: Lively 6/8 instrumental dance-piece closing Persian classical performances
card.profile: Reng is the rhythmic instrumental dance-piece form of Persian classical music - a lively metric composition, almost always in 6/8, performed at the conclusion of a dastgah performance (Persian traditional music, Wikipedia). A typical classical suite proceeds through pishdaramad, chaharmezrab, avaz, tasnif and ends with a reng (Persian traditional music, Wikipedia). Each dastgah has its own characteristic reng; the piece may be improvised or composed for one or more instruments, and is the principal dance form in the radif repertoire (Center for Iranian Music). Historically the reng was accompanied by 'Persian court dance' (raghs-e darbari) (Nasehpour).
card.insight: The reng underpins much of Persian solo improvisational dance; raqs-e tehrani and Persian classical dance are largely improvised to the 6/8 reng rhythm (Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Dance').
